title: Customer SLA-Embedded Security Escalation Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: enterprise customers submit security & compliance asks (SOC2/ISO, GDPR/DPA, HIPAA in narrow cases, vendor questionnaires) during procurement. Current handling is manual: slow, inconsistent SLAs, and poor correlation between ask severity and onboarding gating. Business impact: long sales cycles, surprise contractual requirements, and untracked remediation work for Product and Infra teams.

Goal: deliver a concise playbook and automation baseline that embeds SLA targets into security ask classification and onboarding gating. The playbook will: (1) classify incoming security requests into severity lanes (info, low, medium, high) determined by customer profile + feature surface; (2) tie each lane to baked SLAs, required evidence templates, and remediation windows; (3) automatically route low/medium asks to self-serve evidence collectors and docs, while escalating high asks to Security/Legal with a templated handoff; (4) surface SLA exposure in the onboarding dashboard and trigger billing/credits rules when SLAs are missed.

Scope (MVP): SOC2/ISO basics, GDPR/DPA flagging, standard vendor questionnaires (SIG, CAIQ). Exclude large HIPAA engagements and full contractual redlines in MVP (those route to Legal manually).

Why this approach: aligns sales onboarding commitments with engineering/ops capacity, reduces manual churn by standardizing evidence collection, and makes SLA risk visible to PMs, AE, and CS teams.

Success metrics:
- Median time to first classification action <= 4 hours for inbound requests.
- Reduction in manual Security team triage time by 40% for classified low/medium asks.
- 80% of low/medium asks resolved via self-serve evidence templates within SLA window.
- Sales-led onboarding lead time reduced by 15% for accounts using the playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Automated classifier routes incoming security requests to one of: info, low, medium, high
Each severity lane has a documented SLA and required evidence checklist in Confluence
Low/medium lanes integrate with an evidence collection flow (docs + Drive templates + auto-reminder emails)
High lane creates Security/Legal ticket with pre-populated context (customer profile, impacted products, contract excerpts)
Onboarding dashboard displays live SLA status and a list of open security asks per account
Billing system flag exists to calculate SLA credit when a response SLA is missed (calculation placeholder acceptable for MVP)
tasks: Draft playbook doc with lane definitions and decision thresholds (owner: PM)
Build classifier ruleset prototype (owner: Product/Infra) using keyword heuristics + account risk signals
Create evidence checklist templates for SOC2, ISO, GDPR/DPA, SIG/CAIQ (owner: Security)
Design minimal evidence collection UI and email reminder flow (owner: Console UX)
Implement ticket generation webhook to Security/Legal with structured payload (owner: Eng)
Add SLA widgets to onboarding dashboard and a simple SLA-missed counter (owner: Observability)
Legal & Security review and sign-off on lane definitions and required artifacts
Pilot with two active enterprise accounts and collect feedback
risks_and_tradeoffs: Classifier false positives could gate customers unnecessarily — mitigation: manual override path + audit log
Over-automation may miss nuanced legal asks (e.g., unique contract clauses) — mitigation: escalate to Legal for high-severity lanes
Tight SLAs could create noise and churn on Security team if too aggressive — mitigation: conservative SLA targets for MVP and iterate
Embedding SLA credits into billing requires Finance and Legal involvement; MVP can surface but not fully automate credits
review_feedback: Security (Jamal Patel): prefer conservative defaults for automated gating; require an audit trail for every override (Confluence comment: https://confluence.redwood/team/security/playbooks/pm-314159)

Legal (Marta Rivera): templates OK for evidence; contract redline automation out of scope for MVP — suggested routing + preflight checklist (Drive template: https://drive.redwood/repo/templates/security-evidence-mvp)
Sales (Liam O'Connor): show SLA exposure on the account summary page; AEs want email notifications when a high-severity ask is logged

pilot_plan: Select two accounts with active procurement conversations and a diversity of asks (SOC2/DPA and SIG)
Run playbook in shadow mode for 1 week to compare automated classifications vs manual triage
Enable self-serve evidence flow for low/medium asks for pilot accounts and track completion rate
Hold weekly retros with Security, Legal, Sales and CS to capture friction and adjust lanes
